title: Finite comparison from fs to ordinary fibre products
statement: Let $X,Y,Z$ be locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], let $f:X\to Z$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be log morphisms, and let $W=X\times_ZY$ be the ordinary scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that $W$ is locally Noetherian (this holds for instance when $f$ is finite). Then the fibre product of $f$ and $g$ in locally Noetherian fs log schemes exists; write it $W^{\rm fs}=X\times_Z^{\rm fs}Y$. Its underlying scheme has a canonical finite morphism $c:W^{\rm fs}\to W$, compatible with both projections. If $f$ is Kummer [def-per-kummer-log-morphism], then $c$ is surjective. These statements impose no flatness, strictness, log regularity, or log etaleness hypothesis. The comparison is an isomorphism when one of $f,g$ is strict, meaning that its source log structure is the pullback of its target log structure.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1 (fs conventions), VIII 3.1.17 and 3.2.9, printed pp.101,104 (finite saturation of monoid charts). The fs-product construction and the Kummer surjectivity assertion are an agent formulation of the chart input implicit in X 1.8, p.147; full external reference WANTED in report.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-cospan-compatible-fs-charts] and write $H_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, $S_a=Q_a\amalg_{P_a}R_a$ and $\beta_a:S_a\to A_a$. For an fs test log scheme $T$ with an underlying map $v:T\to H_a$, a pair of log maps to $X,Y$ over $Z$ is exactly a pair of maps $Q_a,R_a\to\Gamma(T,M_T)$ with the given structural images and agreeing on $P_a$. Indeed [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] says chart sections and the forced images of units uniquely determine each log map. The pushout relations therefore identify these pairs with maps $\lambda:S_a\to\Gamma(T,M_T)$ satisfying $\alpha_T\lambda=v^\sharp\beta_a$.

source.place: X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164: pushout chart of the ordinary logarithmic product.

proof.text:
The images of a finite generating set of $S_a$ generate $S_a^{\rm int}$. Its group completion is $S_a^{\rm gp}$, since the defining group relations are unchanged by taking this image. Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation] to $S_a^{\rm int}$: its saturation $S_a^{\rm fs}$ is fs and is a union of finitely many translates $u+S_a^{\rm int}$. Consequently
$$B_a=A_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S_a]}\mathbf Z[S_a^{\rm fs}]$$
is generated over $A_a$ by the finitely many $1\otimes z^u$: write each exponent as $u+s$ and use $1\otimes z^{u+s}=\beta_a(s)(1\otimes z^u)$, choosing a lift $s\in S_a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], $B_a$ is Noetherian. Thus [lem-per-prelog-chart-fs-universal] applies and makes $C_a=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ an fs log scheme representing exactly the pairs of Step 1. Its underlying map to $H_a$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: VIII 3.1.17 and 3.2.9 finiteness sentence; X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164: integral saturated chart and finite comparison.

proof.text: Put $H=\coprod_aH_a$ and $C_H=\coprod_aC_a$. The cover $H\to W$ is fpqc by [lem-per-cospan-compatible-fs-charts]. Over $H\times_WH$, the two strict etale pullbacks of $C_H$ represent the same cone functor. Indeed, on an affine open $U$ of $H_a\times_WH_b$, [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] identifies the restricted log structures of $Z,X,Y$ and of $C_a$ (resp. $C_b$) with those associated to the restricted charts, and the base change of $C_a$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O(U)\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S_a]}\mathbf Z[S_a^{\rm fs}])$; so Step 1 and [lem-per-prelog-chart-fs-universal] apply over $U$ to both, and the local identifications glue by their uniqueness. There is therefore a unique log isomorphism preserving both projections; the two composites of these isomorphisms on a triple overlap agree since both preserve the universal cone, and the composite with its reverse is the identity for the same reason. The underlying morphism $C_H\to H$ is affine (finite on each open-and-closed $H_a$). Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] to obtain a scheme $C\to W$ with this descent datum. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite], and hence locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] on every affine open of $W$.

source.place: X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164; etale descent expanded using Stacks Tags 0245 (descent-lemma-affine) and 02LA (descent-lemma-descending-property-finite).

proof.text: The fs log structures of $C_a$ and their log transition isomorphisms descend to $C$ by [lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent]. Their projections descend on underlying schemes by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] and on inverse-image monoid sheaves by the morphism clause of [lem-trf-fine-log-structure-etale-descent]. Given an fs $T$ and a cone to $X,Y$, its underlying map factors uniquely through $W$. Pull back $H\to W$ to $T$; Step 2 gives unique local log lifts to $C_a$. On double overlaps the lifts agree by the same uniqueness, so these same two descent statements glue them to a unique log lift $T\to C$. Thus $C=W^{\rm fs}$, with canonical finite comparison compatible with both projections.

source.place: VI 1.1 and VIII 3.3.8 final sentence, pp.107--108; X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164, universal-property and descent assembly; Stacks Tag 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms).

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is Kummer. For any geometric point of $W$, choose a lift to some $H_a$ and its algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Evaluation gives $a:Q_a\to\Omega$, $b:R_a\to\Omega$ agreeing on $P_a$. Let $F,E$ be the preimages of the units of the strict local rings at the images in $Z_a,X_a$ under the chart structure maps of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; since an element of a local ring is a unit exactly when its value in $\Omega$ is nonzero, these are the nonzero-evaluation faces of $ah$ and $a$. By [lem-trf-chart-face-localization-logification], the charts induce isomorphisms of $(P_a-F)/F^{\rm gp}$ and $(Q_a-E)/E^{\rm gp}$ with the characteristic monoids at these images, and by chart compatibility $h_a$ induces the characteristic map of $f$. Hence their induced map is injective and root-cofinal by [def-per-kummer-log-morphism]. Apply [lem-per-kummer-sharp-pushout-field-extension] to get $d:S_a^{\rm fs}\to\Omega$. The formula $x\otimes z^u\mapsto x(\bar w)d(u)$ defines a unital ring map $B_a\to\Omega$, since $d(s)=\beta_a(s)(\bar w)$. It gives a point of $C_a$ over the chosen point of $H_a$, hence a point of $C$ over the original point of $W$. Thus $c$ is surjective.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; X 1.8, pp.146--147, Kummer fs-base-change input. Explicit geometric-fibre argument, supplied by agent; no log etaleness used.

proof.text: If $f$ is strict [def-per-strict-log-morphism], the strict clause of [lem-per-cospan-compatible-fs-charts] gives a family of chart neighbourhoods as in Step 1 with $Q_a=P_a$ and $h_a$ the identity; Steps 1--4 apply to it, since $C$ is unique up to unique isomorphism. Then $S_a=Q_a\amalg_{P_a}R_a\simeq R_a$ is already fs, and $B_a=A_a$. The comparison is the identity on every such chart. Over any affine open $W_0\subset W$ take a finite affine chart cover and its disjoint union $H_0\to W_0$; it is flat, surjective and quasi-compact, and the pulled-back comparison is an isomorphism. [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism] makes $c|_{W_0}$ an isomorphism, so $c$ is an isomorphism. Interchanging $X,Y$ proves the assertion when $g$ is strict.

source.place: VI 1.1 and X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164: identity-chart special case; Stacks Tag 02L4 (descent-lemma-descending-property-isomorphism).

proof.text: Finally, if $f$ is finite, the projection $W\to Y$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. On an affine open of the locally Noetherian $Y$, its inverse image has a finite coordinate algebra over a Noetherian ring, which is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. Thus the parenthetical sufficient condition for $W$ holds. The construction in Steps 1--4 uses only fs charts and this local Noetherian condition; the extra Kummer and strict assumptions occur only in Steps 5 and 6.

source.place: VI 1.1 locally Noetherian convention; Stacks Tag 01WL (morphisms-lemma-base-change-finite), and the Noetherian finite-algebra statement cited in lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian.

split_report.summary: Constructs the fs product from integral-saturated pushout charts, reuses finite saturation and exact scheme/log descent statements, proves Kummer surjectivity by a field-valued sharp-pushout lemma, and checks the strict case. Three new statement-only nodes; no Lean writing or compilation. Found explicit source X 3.5 proof Step 6, p.164; no statement change.

tool_uses.why: The associated-log chart universal property turns log maps into maps on generators, an auxiliary log-geometry tool not supplied by the curve-perverse unit.
Finite saturation of a fine monoid, including torsion, is the toric algebra tool needed to make the chart comparison finite.
Finite algebras over Noetherian rings supply the local Noetherian hypotheses for chart construction and descent.
Effective affine scheme descent glues the finite local comparison schemes; the unit has no substitute for scheme descent.
Finiteness is fpqc local on the target, needed after gluing the chart schemes.
Etale descent of fs log structures and arbitrary inverse-image monoid-sheaf maps glues the local cone construction.
The sheaf condition for scheme morphisms glues projections and test lifts.
Identifies the face-localized sharp quotient of a chart with the characteristic monoid at a geometric point; generic log-chart algebra (reviewer FIX, Step 5).
